prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” lawyer for every truck-accident case — the right attorney depends on the details of your case and the lawyer’s experience with commercial trucking claims. I can help you find a strong match. First, here’s how to quickly identify top candidates in Dallas and what to look for when you interview them.

Where to search
- Dallas Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service
- Texas State Bar “Find a Lawyer” and the State Bar disciplinary lookup (to check records)
- Lawyer-rating services: Super Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell (peer review), Avvo, Best Lawyers
- Lists of board-certified attorneys from the Texas Board of Legal Specialization (look for “Personal Injury Trial Law”)
- Local trial lawyer groups and trucking-accident practice groups (trial lawyer associations often highlight experienced plaintiffs’ attorneys)

Key qualifications and experience to look for
- Specific experience handling commercial truck (not just auto) accident cases
- Experience against trucking companies, leasing companies, and their insurers
- Knowledge of FMCSA regulations, hours-of-service, maintenance logs, ELD data, driver qualification files
- Proven track record of verdicts/settlements in truck cases (ask for examples)
- Trial experience — many truck cases are complex and may need to be tried
- Adequate resources/staff (investigators, accident reconstructionists, medical experts)
- Board certification in Personal Injury Trial Law (if applicable) is a plus
- Good client communication and responsiveness
- No serious disciplinary actions

Questions to ask at an initial (often free) consultation
- How many truck-accident cases have you handled? How many in the last 2–3 years?
- Have you handled cases against large trucking companies/insurers? What were outcomes?
- Do you try cases? What percentage go to trial vs settle?
- What is your approach to investigating a trucking crash (use of reconstruction, data download, expert witnesses)?
- Who will handle the case day-to-day (partner, associate)?
- What are your fees and costs? (contingency %, what expenses I’d be responsible for)
- How will you communicate updates and how often?
- Can you provide references or examples of verdicts/settlements?

Red flags
- No experience with truck-specific evidence (ELD/downloads, driver logs)
- Promises of a specific result
- Poor communication during the intake process
- Unclear or unusually high fee terms

What to prepare before a consultation
- Police report, photos/videos of the scene and damages, medical records/ bills, insurance information, any correspondence with insurers, witness information, employer info for the truck driver (if known)

If you want, I can:
- Draft an email/phone script to contact several attorneys
- Provide a short checklist you can use in consultations
- Help narrow choices if you give me a few lawyers/firms you’ve found (I can point out things to verify)

Would you like me to draft a script or help compile a shortlist of Dallas lawyers based on specific criteria (trial experience, board certification, client ratings)?
